hlni.insight: Specific tasks cannot be definitively assigned to a degree without verified curriculum documents.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles imply universal, fixed task lists.
hlni.viewerChange: Shifts from guessing based on stereotypes to requesting specific learning objective documents.
hlni.support: Logical reasoning: In the absence of institutional documentation (the missing link), any classification is an unsupported assumption.
hlni.payoff: The viewer stops guessing and learns to ask for objective evidence.

candidate.reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Missing Link
candidate.creativeAngle: Using a forced-choice challenge to demonstrate that without clear documentation, assigning a specific task to a degree is impossible.
candidate.objective: Teach students to identify missing information instead of guessing based on stereotypes.
candidate.targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Challenge Setup
shots.visual: Presenter holds a card titled 'Example: Task: Audit Budget | Degree: ?'.
shots.dialogue: Everyone says B.Com or BBA determines your career. But look at this task: Audit Budget. Which degree owns it?
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the card, then the presenter looking skeptical.

shots.name: The Reveal
shots.visual: Presenter shakes head, placing the card down firmly.
shots.dialogue: Actually? You cannot know. Without a syllabus linking the task to the curriculum, you are just guessing.
shots.cameraPerformance: Cut to a wider shot showing the empty space where the degree label should be.

shots.name: The Actionable Question
shots.visual: Presenter points to an imaginary document on screen.
shots.dialogue: Stop guessing based on myths. Instead, ask: What document shows the specific course learning objectives for this?
shots.onscreenText: What document shows the specific course learning objectives for this?
shots.cameraPerformance: Direct eye contact, calm and practical.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Reframing a degree comparison as an evidence-based investigation rather than a guessing game.

selected.title: The Missing Link Challenge
selected.audienceGap: Assuming a specific business example belongs to one degree over the other.
selected.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
selected.viewerChange: Recognizes that context, not the example itself, defines its disciplinary home.
selected.concept: Presenting an example of a budget report and challenging the viewer to assign it.
selected.device: A quick-fire quiz where the 'correct' answer is that there isn't enough info.
selected.support: This is a reasoning limit: absent information cannot establish an exclusive classification.
methodSteps: Present one example without a source linking it to a category.
Separate a plausible guess from what the available information proves.
Identify the exact missing source or information needed to decide.
selected.interpretationRule: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.visibleProof: A forced-choice guess is replaced by a justified third answer and a precise request for missing evidence.
selected.payoff: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.limitations: Do not assert that the example belongs to both degrees, or to either one, without actual curriculum evidence.

demonstration.observation: No supplied source connects this example to either category; the supported result is insufficient information.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What document shows the specific course learning objectives for this?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of a blank worksheet being filled out while narrating the need for specific criteria.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: Natural, informal conversation between two peers using a shared notebook.
